statistics.analysis_plan.value: Primary outcome: Recorded symptom-score change, follow-up minus baseline, on 0–100, using the selected baseline and Days 45–90 score. Negative change means symptom reduction; positive change means worsening. Include people with both selected scores. Report the contributing number of people, mean change, standard deviation, 95% confidence interval, median and range. Secondary outcome 1: Proportion with at least a 20-point decrease in the same score. Denominator: people with both selected scores; numerator: change <= -20. This is a supplied descriptive threshold, not a validated responder definition or a guarantee of meaningful clinical benefit. Secondary outcome 2: Number of documented clinician-directed dry eye care changes per person on Days 1–90 after index. Report counts using the stated event rules. Report separately those with a supported zero count and those whose care-change status is unknown. Use people with sufficient care documentation as the analysis denominator; report that denominator explicitly. Exploratory outcome: Association of index contact-lens status with paired symptom change. Compare documented wearers and documented nonwearers using a linear model adjusted for baseline symptom score and age. Report the wearer-minus-nonwearer adjusted difference with a 95% confidence interval. Unknown status remains in cohort summaries but is excluded from this comparison; report its count and reason. Use available observed values. Do not impute symptoms, contact-lens status or care changes. Distinguish missing, ambiguous and explicitly absent information. Describe availability and reasons for missingness for each endpoint. Missing scores do not remove a person from the overall cohort or unrelated summaries. There are no prospective safety endpoints, confirmatory significance claims, additional exploratory outcomes or causal conclusions. Selection, documentation, attendance and confounding limit interpretation.

After the required permissions, staff verify eligibility, deduplicate records, assign study IDs and abstract age at index, sex, index date, documented contact-lens status, the ordinary-care plan, recorded symptom ratings with dates, and subsequent clinician-directed care changes. Original records remain at the clinic. The clinic's existing symptom field asks: 'Over the past seven days, how severe were your dry eye symptoms overall?' It uses 0, no symptoms, through 100, worst imaginable symptoms. Higher is worse. No validation claim is supplied. Use only that recorded scale; do not convert other questionnaires, infer a rating from narrative notes or treat absent scores as zero. For baseline, use the latest eligible score in Days -14 through 0. A Day 0 score must be explicitly recorded before the index care decision; otherwise it is not an eligible baseline. If multiple scores occur on the selected date, use the latest time-stamped eligible score. If ordering cannot be resolved, mark the baseline as ambiguous and missing rather than choosing arbitrarily. For follow-up, select the eligible score closest to historical Day 60 within Days 45 through 90; ties between dates use the earlier date. If multiple scores occur on that date, use the last time-stamped score. If times cannot resolve multiple values, mark that outcome value ambiguous and missing. Retain the care received as documented. Recorded change does not estimate an untreated symptom trajectory or prove that index care was effective.

Contact-lens status has three categories: explicitly documented wearer, explicitly documented nonwearer, and unknown/not documented. Do not infer wear from a prescription or collapse unknown into nonwearer.

A care change is a clinician-directed start, stop or dose-frequency change of dry eye medication or a clinician-directed start/stop of a non-drug dry eye care measure. A refill alone, appointment booking or administrative note is not a care change. Count one coordinated adjustment on the same date as one event, even when several measures change. Deduplicate reports by patient, date and clinical event; retain an uncertain event as uncertain, not a definite change. A zero-change count requires explicit documentation that care remained unchanged covering the interval. Absence of a subsequent record alone is unknown, not zero.

Baseline selection window: Days -14 through 0 relative to that encounter. Historical Day 60 outcome selection window: Days 45 through 90 after index. Care-change observation window: Days 1 through 90 after index. These are record-selection windows, not scheduled visits or a requirement for people to attend at those times. All clinical data predate research abstraction. Staff will not contact people or arrange new care to fill gaps.

POPULATION, ELIGIBILITY AND SAMPLE Include all eligible records; anticipate 180 unique adults at the single site. The person is the enrollment and analysis unit. The symptom rating concerns both eyes together; no eye-level cohort, separate-eye outcome or paired-eye model is specified. Multiple encounters for one person do not create new participants. Age: 18 through 85 years inclusive at the index encounter. All sexes eligible. Healthy volunteers: No. Sampling: Consecutive eligible records in the fixed period. Inclusion criteria: - Age 18 through 85 at index. - Clinician-documented dry eye disease. - A routine-care encounter during the index period documenting a dry eye care plan, including an explicitly documented decision to continue existing care. - Accessible records identifying the person and index date reliably. - Access authorized by the site and required ethics/privacy decisions. Use only the first qualifying index encounter per person. Deduplicate records using the clinic's patient identifier before assigning a study ID. Exclusion criteria: - The person or index date cannot be reliably established after source verification. - The putative index encounter was part of an interventional research protocol, rather than ordinary clinical care. Missing symptom scores, uncertain contact-lens status and incomplete subsequent care documentation do not exclude an otherwise eligible person. They affect only the relevant analysis denominator. Prior surgery, medication use and ordinary-care changes are recorded characteristics, not automatic exclusions. There is no research screening, nonparticipation interval, washout or restriction on other research participation. Pregnancy status is not collected and creates no eligibility restriction. No child records are included. Sample justification: All eligible records in the fixed index period constitute the sample; 180 people is a feasibility estimate. Report actual counts and exclusions. There is no formal power calculation, assumed effect size, recruitment quota or prospective loss-to-follow-up allowance.

ABSTRACTION AND SELECTION RULES After the required permissions, staff verify eligibility, deduplicate records, assign study IDs and abstract age at index, sex, index date, documented contact-lens status, the ordinary-care plan, recorded symptom ratings with dates, and subsequent clinician-directed care changes. Original records remain at the clinic. The clinic's existing symptom field asks: 'Over the past seven days, how severe were your dry eye symptoms overall?' It uses 0, no symptoms, through 100, worst imaginable symptoms. Higher is worse. No validation claim is supplied. Use only that recorded scale; do not convert other questionnaires, infer a rating from narrative notes or treat absent scores as zero. For baseline, use the latest eligible score in Days -14 through 0. A Day 0 score must be explicitly recorded before the index care decision; otherwise it is not an eligible baseline. If multiple scores occur on the selected date, use the latest time-stamped eligible score. If ordering cannot be resolved, mark the baseline as ambiguous and missing rather than choosing arbitrarily. For follow-up, select the eligible score closest to historical Day 60 within Days 45 through 90; ties between dates use the earlier date. If multiple scores occur on that date, use the last time-stamped score. If times cannot resolve multiple values, mark that outcome value ambiguous and missing. Retain the care received as documented. Recorded change does not estimate an untreated symptom trajectory or prove that index care was effective. Contact-lens status has three categories: explicitly documented wearer, explicitly documented nonwearer, and unknown/not documented. Do not infer wear from a prescription or collapse unknown into nonwearer. A care change is a clinician-directed start, stop or dose-frequency change of dry eye medication or a clinician-directed start/stop of a non-drug dry eye care measure. A refill alone, appointment booking or administrative note is not a care change. Count one coordinated adjustment on the same date as one event, even when several measures change. Deduplicate reports by patient, date and clinical event; retain an uncertain event as uncertain, not a definite change. A zero-change count requires explicit documentation that care remained unchanged covering the interval. Absence of a subsequent record alone is unknown, not zero. No new examination, pressure or vision test, questionnaire, telephone call, clinic visit, specimen collection, genetic test or imaging re-reading is performed. There is no specimen transfer, storage, banking or future specimen use.

OUTCOMES AND ANALYSIS Primary outcome: Recorded symptom-score change, follow-up minus baseline, on 0–100, using the selected baseline and Days 45–90 score. Negative change means symptom reduction; positive change means worsening. Include people with both selected scores. Report the contributing number of people, mean change, standard deviation, 95% confidence interval, median and range. Secondary outcome 1: Proportion with at least a 20-point decrease in the same score. Denominator: people with both selected scores; numerator: change <= -20. This is a supplied descriptive threshold, not a validated responder definition or a guarantee of meaningful clinical benefit. Secondary outcome 2: Number of documented clinician-directed dry eye care changes per person on Days 1–90 after index. Report counts using the stated event rules. Report separately those with a supported zero count and those whose care-change status is unknown. Use people with sufficient care documentation as the analysis denominator; report that denominator explicitly. Exploratory outcome: Association of index contact-lens status with paired symptom change. Compare documented wearers and documented nonwearers using a linear model adjusted for baseline symptom score and age. Report the wearer-minus-nonwearer adjusted difference with a 95% confidence interval. A positive difference means less symptom reduction or more worsening among documented wearers, not proof of harm from lenses. Unknown status remains in cohort summaries but is excluded from this comparison; report its count and reason. Use available observed values. Do not impute symptoms, contact-lens status or care changes. Distinguish missing, ambiguous and explicitly absent information. Describe availability and reasons for missingness for each endpoint. Missing scores do not remove a person from the overall cohort or unrelated summaries. There are no prospective safety endpoints, confirmatory significance claims, additional exploratory outcomes or causal conclusions. Selection, documentation, attendance and confounding limit interpretation.

RISKS, BENEFITS, PAYMENT AND CARE Research risk is loss of confidentiality from record access and linkage. The research performs no new physical intervention or assessment. Secure access, separate keys and aggregate reporting mitigate privacy risk. No direct benefit to people whose records are reviewed is expected; findings may inform future research and documentation practices. Ordinary care is unaffected. There is no recruitment, consent appointment, participant payment, compensation, travel reimbursement, new clinical charge or research treatment. The sponsor pays staff abstraction and analysis costs. No new research-injury treatment program or insurance promise is established for this records-only project. The investigator handles suspected privacy incidents under site policy and applicable ethics/privacy reporting requirements; no study-specific reporting hour count has been supplied. Do not invent physical adverse-event collection, follow-up examinations or new contact obligations.

ETHICS, PRIVACY AND RECORDS Requested review body: Northfield Independent Research Ethics Board. Request waivers of informed consent and privacy authorization for the records-only review. The application will describe privacy protections and the burden and selection bias of recontacting former clinic patients. No waiver or approval is currently granted. If permissions are not granted, the investigator must obtain an authorized revised study plan before research access; this document does not authorize a switch to contacting patients. Authorized site research staff access identifying source records and perform linkage within the clinic's encrypted access-controlled environment. The identity key is stored separately from the coded dataset. Signed access agreements and abstraction logs remain at the clinic. Analysts and sponsor receive coded data only, with age at index and relative-day intervals rather than names, contact details, birth dates or exact clinical dates. Exact dates remain in restricted site records for eligibility and window verification. No Social Security numbers or genetic information are abstracted. Authorized monitors, the reviewing IRB and legally authorized oversight bodies may inspect relevant original records for oversight. Reports contain aggregate results; suppress public cells with fewer than five people and complementary cells that would reveal the suppressed count. Do not publish individual-level data or identifying case descriptions. Retain the coded study dataset, identity key, access approvals and abstraction logs securely for five years after administrative closeout on 30 June 2027, then destroy research copies unless a binding requirement requires longer. Original clinical records follow the clinic's separate ordinary retention policy; the study does not order their destruction. No sale, public individual-data sharing, unrelated future research, commercial specimens or banking is planned. Because this protocol requests a waiver and has no direct participation, there is no participant signature process or prospective withdrawal visit. Any site privacy request is handled through the site and applicable permissions, without promising that previously deidentified aggregate analyses can be reversed.

STAFF WORK PLAN AND COMPLETION November 2026: Obtain required approvals and site access permission, verify record availability and eligibility, and deduplicate the cohort. December 2026 through February 2027: Abstract and verify historical records. March 2027: Resolve permitted source queries and lock the coded dataset. April through May 2027: Analyze and prepare aggregate findings. Administrative closeout: 30 June 2027, with reconciliation and secure archiving. These are future staff tasks, not new clinical data collection, enrollment, follow-up visits or recruitment dates. Do not extend the historical record period. A record's abstraction is complete when required extraction and permitted queries are resolved, including explicit missing/ambiguous codes. Study completion occurs when the coded dataset is locked and planned analyses/reporting are complete; administrative archiving ends by 30 June 2027. Unavailable source data are reported, not replaced with participant recontact or new tests. The investigator may suspend research access if a required permission is withdrawn or a privacy incident requires suspension under site policy. Preserve legally required records and obtain the required authorization before resuming. Do not add participant-level clinical stopping criteria to this records-only review.

study.background: Existing records may describe symptoms and subsequent care, but clinic attendance, questionnaire completeness and prescribing documentation vary. The clinic lacks a combined account that separates recorded symptom change from missing follow-up and undocumented care changes. study.hypothesis: Hypothesis: People explicitly documented as contact-lens wearers will have a smaller recorded symptom reduction than people explicitly documented as nonwearers. This is an exploratory association hypothesis, not an established effect or a claim that contact lenses or any treatment caused the observed changes.
